name: Ubiquiti Inc.
moat_justification: UniFi single-pane ecosystem switching costs across networking/Protect/Access/NAS and a structural lean cost advantage (no direct sales force, no licensing model, SBC of $7,444,000 against OCF of $928,682,000; operating income $1,185,442,000 in FY2026) with proven pricing power — against no recurring revenue, no white-glove enterprise support, copycat license-free rivals (TP-Link Omada), ~93% founder ownership/key-man risk with a tiny float, and East-Asia supply/tariff exposure with flagged component cost pressure.
fragility_flags: BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 14.88 vs 3-yr median 10.25 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.7x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Elite lean hardware franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $620.24 the weighted IRR is only 9.85% with IV@15% of $326.30, and even the super-bull case barely clears 15%; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$326, or ~$235 with a margin of safety.
moat_for: UniFi ecosystem switching costs: single pane of glass across networking, Protect, Access and NAS; rip-out means replacing the whole stack
Structural cost advantage: no direct sales force, no licensing-fee model, near-zero SBC supports high margins while undercutting Cisco/Fortinet TCO
Proven pricing power: operating income rose from $836,280,000 (FY2025) to $1,185,442,000 (FY2026)
Capital discipline: long-term debt eliminated by FY2025, $1.00/quarter dividend initiated, buybacks executed when the stock was cheap
moat_against: No recurring revenue: one-off hardware re-won every refresh cycle, no subscription/licensing annuity
No white-glove enterprise support: hard ceiling on Fortune 500 penetration
License-free model is copyable at the low end: TP-Link Omada and others mimic the playbook
Key-man/governance concentration: founder owns ~93%, no earnings calls or guidance, tiny float manufactures volatility
East-Asia contract manufacturing: tariff, supply and component-cost exposure (flagged in Q4 FY2026 coverage)
Service Provider Technology in decline: growth is single-engine (Enterprise Technology)
